summary: Judge whether the vendor-declared resilience mechanisms suit network and power outages and meet their declared guarantees.

units.note: Combined declared mechanisms judged against declared guarantees.
Each declared mechanism judged against its own description.

outside_procedure_cues: Reconnection and event-replay bursts after natural WAN or power outages hint at buffering or retry mechanisms, but not their declared guarantees.
rationale: Both criteria assess the adequacy of mechanisms against guarantees that exist only in the IXIT; nothing observable substitutes for the declared design.

summary: Cut network and power to the device and check resilience mechanisms behave as the vendor declared.

units.note: Tester interrupts network link and compares behaviour with declaration.
Tester interrupts power and compares behaviour with declaration.

outside_procedure_cues: During natural outages the gateway sees reconnect timing, DHCP re-requests and queued uploads after restoration; these cannot be matched to declared behaviour.
rationale: The only verdict bullet is a difference from the IXIT documentation (R1), and the procedure also requires causing outages.

summary: Judge declared resilience mechanisms for staying locally functional offline and recovering cleanly after power loss.

units.note: Repeats 5.9-1-1 units on declared mechanisms.
Declared network-outage mechanisms judged for keeping local operation.
Declared power-outage mechanisms judged for clean recovery.

outside_procedure_cues: Post-outage traffic shows whether the device reconnects at all, which hints at recovery design but not at the declared mechanism types.
rationale: Every bullet is an appropriateness judgement of mechanisms that are known only from the IXIT; observed behaviour belongs to the functional case.

summary: Interrupt network and power; check behaviour matches declaration, local operation continues, and connectivity and function resume.

units.note: Tester cuts network, compares with declaration, checks local functionality.
Tester cuts power, compares with declaration, checks resumed state.

outside_procedure_cues: Declared-behaviour comparison unusable; observed reconnect delays and replayed event uploads could only be compared with expectations, not the IXIT.
rationale: Bullet one compares with the IXIT and is dropped (R1). After a natural outage, failure to rejoin DHCP or the cloud shows a non-recovery indication; local function and same state cannot be shown, so no PASS.

assumptions: a natural network or power outage was correctly identified from traffic
missing reconnection reflects a device fault, not user disconnection
LAN traffic during WAN loss reflects local functionality
a natural network or power outage was correctly identified from traffic
missing reconnection reflects a device fault, not user disconnection
LAN traffic during WAN loss reflects local functionality

summary: Judge whether each network interface's resilience measures give orderly, standards-following connection and avoid mass reconnection storms.

units.note: Declared measures for orderly connection; observable as handshake/DHCP conformance.
Declared measures for network stability; observable as retry backoff and jitter.

outside_procedure_cues: Fleet-level load balancing or batched update notifications are invisible from one home.
rationale: Criteria are properties (orderly, standard-conformant, no mass reconnection). Substituting observed reconnection behaviour, tight retry loops or non-conformant setup show FAIL; completeness across interfaces and fleet measures prevent PASS.

assumptions: observed connection behaviour reflects the measures the IXIT would list
observed interfaces cover all network-accessible logical interfaces
repeated reconnections reveal whether delays are randomized
observed connection behaviour reflects the measures the IXIT would list
observed interfaces cover all network-accessible logical interfaces
repeated reconnections reveal whether delays are randomized

summary: Check implemented resilience measures per network interface work as declared, especially against simultaneous mass reconnection.

units.note: Tester sniffs connection setup and compares with declared measures.

outside_procedure_cues: Handshake/teardown conformance, retry intervals and backoff after outages are all observable passively, but only usable against the declared measures.
rationale: The sole verdict bullet is a difference from the IXIT documentation (R1), even though the procedure itself is sniffer-based.

summary: Check the vendor examines collected telemetry for security anomalies and that the telemetry suits that examination.

units.note: Existence of at least one declared security examination.
Declared telemetry judged suitable for the declared examination.

outside_procedure_cues: Periodic uploads to vendor telemetry or logging endpoints show telemetry exists, but not whether anyone examines it.
rationale: Examination happens at the manufacturer's back end; its existence and suitability are known only from the IXIT.

summary: Judge that a simple user function erases all user data, including personal data, configuration and cryptographic material, from the device.

units.note: Simple erase function for a non-expert; public manual may describe reset.
Adequacy of each erase function to remove the targeted data.
Coverage of personal data, configuration and keys.

outside_procedure_cues: Post-reset traffic reusing user-set hostnames or account sessions would hint at incomplete erasure but is not used here.
rationale: User data storage is evident (device holds home network settings). If public documentation offers no simple erase function, FAIL can be inferred; adequacy and coverage are internal, so no PASS.

assumptions: published documentation lists every erase function the device offers
joining the home network implies stored user configuration

summary: Create user data, run each erase function, check interaction matches declaration, data is gone, and users cannot erase others' data.

units.note: Tester creates typical user data.
Tester runs erase and compares interaction with declaration.
Check leftover data after erasure; persistence may leak into traffic.
Multi-user cross-deletion attempt.

outside_procedure_cues: Interaction-consistency bullet unusable; observed reset sequence (re-provisioning traffic) could otherwise be compared with the declared flow.
rationale: Interaction bullet compares with the IXIT (R1). After an opportunistic user reset, user-set names or account tokens still visible in traffic indicate non-erasure; erasure success and multi-user rules need interaction.

assumptions: a user-initiated full erasure happened in the observed window
identifiers persisting after reset are user data, not factory data
a user-initiated full erasure happened in the observed window
identifiers persisting after reset are user data, not factory data

summary: Judge that simple device-side functions let users delete personal data from every associated service that stores it.

units.note: Existence of a simple deletion function; public docs may describe account deletion.
Coverage of all storing services; contacted services observable via DNS/SNI.

rationale: Associated services can be enumerated from DNS/SNI and public documents substituted for declared functions; an observed storing service with no documented deletion path shows FAIL. Full coverage is unverifiable, so no PASS.

assumptions: contacted services actually store personal data
published documentation lists every deletion function
observed endpoints include all associated services

summary: Create personal data on services, run each removal, check interaction matches declaration and data is gone from services.

units.note: Tester creates personal data on associated services.
Tester runs removal and compares interaction with declaration.
Tester checks service data/accounts after removal.

outside_procedure_cues: Continued encrypted sessions to the same service after a user's deletion request hint at remaining accounts but reveal nothing about stored data.
rationale: Interaction bullet compares with the IXIT (R1); remaining data on remote services is hidden by TLS and server-side storage, so no indication is obtainable.

summary: Check user instructions cover every deletion function and give concise, complete steps to delete personal data.

units.note: Tester creates personal data on device and services.
Declared deletion functions checked against published documentation.
Tester follows documented steps; conciseness judged from documents.

outside_procedure_cues: Coverage bullet unusable: comparing published instructions with the declared function list needs the IXIT.
rationale: Coverage compares with the IXIT list (R1). Conciseness and step completeness are document properties; missing or verbose public instructions show FAIL, but completeness requires performing the steps, so no PASS.

assumptions: published documentation is the documentation the IXIT references
missing steps can be judged without performing them

summary: Run each deletion function and check the user receives a clear confirmation that the data was deleted.

units.note: Tester creates personal data on associated services.
Tester performs each documented deletion.
Tester inspects confirmation shown to user.

rationale: The confirmation is a user-interface message after a deletion the observer cannot trigger; its clarity is invisible in network traffic.

summary: Judge that each user installation or maintenance decision is necessary and that its default follows security best practice.

units.note: Necessity of each declared decision; manual may list setup choices.
Defaults judged against EN 303 645; default-on services observable in traffic.

rationale: Defaults are a property judged against EN 303 645 guidance. Default UPnP port mappings, plaintext services or remote access seen out of the box show FAIL; necessity of all decisions cannot be shown, so no PASS.

assumptions: observed behaviour reflects default settings, not user changes
observed behaviour corresponds to a user decision the IXIT would list
observed behaviour reflects default settings, not user changes
observed behaviour corresponds to a user decision the IXIT would list

summary: Trigger each user decision; check it is prominent, understandable to non-experts, and as declared.

units.note: Tester triggers every declared decision.
Prominence in setup/maintenance flows.
Understandability for non-experts.
Conformance with declared description and options.

outside_procedure_cues: Setup-phase traffic (provisioning access point, pairing bursts) marks when decisions occur but not how they are presented.
rationale: Prominence and understandability are user-interface properties needing interaction; the conformance bullet compares with the IXIT (R1).

summary: Set up per published secure-setup guide; check it covers every security-relevant decision with a recommendation.

units.note: Tester sets up device following the guide.
Coverage of declared security-relevant decisions by the guide.
Guide gives recommendations for those decisions.

outside_procedure_cues: Coverage bullet unusable as written; observed security-relevant features (UPnP, local APIs) absent from the guide would otherwise indicate gaps.
rationale: Coverage compares with the IXIT decision list (R1). Recommendations are a document property: a security-relevant choice in the public guide without a recommendation shows FAIL; completeness unknown, so no PASS.

assumptions: security-relevant decisions identified from public documents and traffic match those the IXIT lists

summary: Judge that published guidance covers every step and parameter for checking secure setup and secure maintained state.

units.note: Setup-check documentation assessed for covering needed steps.
Maintenance-check documentation assessed for covering needed steps.

rationale: Guidance is public, so its absence or obvious gaps show FAIL; knowing every necessary step requires device configuration knowledge, so PASS is out of reach.

assumptions: published guidance is the documentation the IXIT references
needed check steps are inferable without device knowledge

summary: Apply the documented checks to a secure and a deliberately insecure configuration; checks must classify both correctly.

units.note: Tester configures a secure example setup.
Apply documented setup check.
Apply documented maintenance check.
Tester configures an insecure setup.
Repeat checks.

outside_procedure_cues: Traffic can independently reveal insecure states (plaintext services, outdated firmware banners) that a correct user check should flag.
rationale: Requires configuring the device into known states and running the checks; the observer can do neither.

summary: Check every user interface has a declared input validation method effective against manipulation and failures.

units.note: Each declared user interface has a declared validation method.
Effectiveness of declared methods for user-interface input.

rationale: User-interface input and its validation are internal and declared only in the IXIT; nothing passes the gateway.

summary: Check all user interfaces are declared and that validation rejects unexpected input, e.g. by fuzzing or web scanning.

units.note: Discovered user interfaces compared with declared list.
Tester feeds unexpected input to each interface.

outside_procedure_cues: A plaintext web UI seen in traffic reveals interfaces and error pages but not validation behaviour.
rationale: Interface-list bullet compares with the IXIT (R1); validation evidence needs injecting malformed input, which is active.

summary: Check every network-accessible logical interface has a declared input validation method effective against manipulation and failures.

units.note: Each declared network interface has a declared validation method.
Effectiveness of declared methods for network input.

outside_procedure_cues: Observed listening services and protocols identify which interfaces receive network input, without revealing validation.
rationale: Both criteria evaluate declared methods; observed interfaces cannot substitute for knowledge of validation logic.

summary: Fuzz network interfaces to check validation rejects unexpected input; check all network interfaces are declared.

units.note: Tester sends unexpected input; device reaction observable.
Discovered network interfaces compared with declared list.

outside_procedure_cues: Interface-documentation bullet unusable; observed open services could otherwise be compared with the declared interface list.
rationale: Documentation bullet compares with the IXIT (R1). If third-party malformed input is followed by crash or error leakage, a FAIL indication exists; without own probing, PASS cannot be claimed.

assumptions: observed inbound malformed traffic caused the device failure
a crash or reboot is correctly inferred from traffic
observed inbound malformed traffic caused the device failure
a crash or reboot is correctly inferred from traffic

summary: Judge that consumer information clearly states what personal data is processed, why, by whom and for how long.

units.note: Privacy information judged per declared category; recipients cross-checkable with observed destinations.

rationale: The information is public and judged on content: missing purposes, recipients or retention, or observed third-party recipients not named, show FAIL. Unknown categories prevent PASS.

assumptions: the public privacy policy is the information provided to consumers
flows to unlisted parties carry personal data

summary: Check the consumer information on personal data processing is clear and transparent and matches the declaration.

units.note: Clarity and transparency of provided information per category.
Provided information compared with declared description.

outside_procedure_cues: Match-with-declaration bullet unusable; observed destinations and plaintext fields could otherwise be set against the declared processing.
rationale: The IXIT-match bullet is dropped (R1). Clarity is a property of public information; unclear text or undisclosed observed recipients show FAIL, while per-category completeness blocks PASS.

assumptions: the public privacy policy is the information provided to consumers
observed destinations represent personal data recipients

summary: Judge that consent for consent-based processing is described and given as a free, obvious, explicit opt-in.

units.note: Declared consent method judged; transmissions before setup hint at missing opt-in.

rationale: Properties of the opt-in can be substituted by public descriptions and setup-time traffic; transmissions to analytics before any opt-in show FAIL. Validity of consent cannot be confirmed, so no PASS.

assumptions: the processing observed before setup is consent-based
the flow before setup carries personal data

summary: Check consent for each consent-based processing is obtained as declared.

units.note: Tester walks consent flow and compares with declaration.

outside_procedure_cues: Analytics or advertising traffic beginning before setup completes would indicate processing without opt-in, but is not usable here.
rationale: The sole bullet is a match with the declared description (R1).

summary: Judge that it is described how to withdraw consent at any time by configuring device and services.

units.note: Declared withdrawal description; public documents may describe it.

rationale: Description of withdrawal is a document property; if public documents describe no withdrawal means, FAIL can be inferred. Adequacy of the declared description cannot be confirmed, so no PASS.

assumptions: published documentation contains every withdrawal means the device offers

summary: Check consent can be withdrawn in the declared way for each consent-based processing.

units.note: Tester withdraws consent and compares with declaration.

outside_procedure_cues: Analytics flows persisting after a user withdraws consent would be a strong cue, but cannot be used.
rationale: The sole bullet compares with the declared withdrawal description (R1), and withdrawal requires interaction.

summary: Judge that the device provides a means of storing consent information for consent-based processing.

units.note: Declared consent-storage means on device or associated service.

rationale: Consent records are stored internally or server-side; encrypted traffic cannot distinguish them, so neither outcome is reachable.

summary: Check the storage of consent information matches its declared description.

units.note: Consent storage compared with declaration.

rationale: The verdict is a mismatch with the declared description (R1).

summary: Judge that personal data within telemetry is necessary for the stated purpose of collection.

units.note: Necessity of declared telemetry personal data; plaintext telemetry fields observable.

rationale: Necessity relative to purpose is a property; plaintext telemetry carrying identifiers unrelated to the public purpose shows FAIL. Encrypted content and unknown categories prevent PASS.

assumptions: observed payload is telemetry
manufacturer-stated purpose stands in for the IXIT-declared purpose

summary: Judge whether the documentation on telemetry lets consumers obtain information about telemetry processing.

units.note: Suitability of telemetry documentation for consumers.

outside_procedure_cues: Observed telemetry endpoints confirm telemetry exists, strengthening a missing-documentation finding.
rationale: Documentation is public; its absence or unusability shows FAIL. Suitability depends on what telemetry is actually collected, which is only partly observable, so no PASS.

assumptions: published documentation is the telemetry documentation the IXIT references

summary: Check telemetry information is obtainable as declared, matches declared purposes, and fully describes data, use, recipients and purposes.

units.note: Obtained information compared with declared documentation.
Obtained information compared with declared purposes.
Information describes the telemetry collected.
Information describes use, recipients and purposes.

outside_procedure_cues: Bullets on matching the declaration are unusable; observed telemetry could otherwise be compared with declared purposes.
rationale: Two bullets compare with the IXIT (R1). Observed telemetry or recipients missing from public information show FAIL under the completeness bullets; completeness itself cannot be confirmed.

assumptions: observed flows to telemetry endpoints are telemetry
public information is the information provided to consumers

Reasonableness of declared retention.

observed data is personal data
